examples.title: Source and target IDs are positional

limitations: Only high-risk groups of bare `str`, `int`, or `float` annotations are reported.
Tests, generated code, protocols, routes, CLI handlers, overrides, and conventional ordered pairs are excluded.
rules.rationale: Callers can exchange semantically distinct positional values without a type-checking failure.
rules.remediation: Insert `*` before the risky parameters and pass them by name at call sites.
rules.summary: Swap-prone parameters with the same primitive type should be keyword-only.

examples.title: Concrete service directly exposes an injected collaborator
Service implements a declared port

limitations: This advisory uses service-family names, constructor annotations, collaborator calls, and public-method counts as heuristics.
Tests, generated code, scripts, known framework shapes, persistence-only dependencies, and classes with declared bases are excluded.
rules.rationale: A small port can decouple consumers when they genuinely need to substitute a concrete service boundary.
rules.remediation: Define a focused `Protocol` or ABC and type substituting consumers against it, or suppress the advisory when no substitution boundary exists.
rules.summary: Consider a consumer-owned port for a service with a behaviorally used collaborator.

examples.title: Docstring repeats the test name
Docstring explains the regression

limitations: Only test functions and unbased Test-prefixed classes in recognized test files are checked.
Structured, protected, value-bearing, generated, and genuinely novel docstrings are preserved.
rules.rationale: A docstring that narrates visible test code creates duplicate prose that can drift without explaining the regression or contract.
rules.remediation: Delete the redundant docstring, improve the test name, or document a reason or constraint not visible in the test.
rules.summary: Test docstrings must add information beyond the test name and body.

examples.title: Private helper appears after its sole caller
Private helper appears before its sole caller

limitations: Generated files, tests, `__main__.py`, mutual recursion, and helpers with multiple callers are excluded.
Decorated definitions and dynamic references that cannot prove a sole caller are not reported.
rules.rationale: Caller-first ordering keeps the module's public flow visible before its implementation details.
rules.remediation: Move the private helper below its sole caller without changing either body.
rules.summary: A private helper used by one caller should be defined below that caller.

limitations: Only SQL string literals in recognized store modules are analyzed.
Named ordinary create methods are excluded because a uniqueness error may be their intended contract.
rules.rationale: A method named as an enqueue, seed, migration, schedule, ensure, or upsert promises replay safety.
rules.remediation: Use `ON CONFLICT`, `ON DUPLICATE KEY`, or SQLite `OR IGNORE`/`OR REPLACE` as appropriate.
rules.summary: Embedded inserts in replay-contract store methods must handle conflicts explicitly.

examples.title: Bare phase label
Comment explains a consequence

limitations: Only standalone comments in recognized test files are checked; nested literal comments and trailing comments are excluded.
Comments containing words beyond the bounded phase-label grammar are preserved.
rules.rationale: Phase labels narrate test structure without explaining behavior and often indicate that a test needs clearer names or smaller units.
rules.remediation: Delete the label; if the phases remain hard to follow, extract a named helper or split the test.
rules.summary: Tests must not use bare Arrange, Act, Assert, Given, When, or Then phase comments.

examples.title: Comment repeats the duration

limitations: Detection targets simple numeric assignments with a trailing comment that repeats the number and unit.
Approximate conversions, reasons, references, directives, bracketed values, and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: A unit encoded only in a comment can drift from the value and is unavailable to type checking.
rules.remediation: Encode the unit in the name or value type, such as timeout_seconds or timedelta.
rules.summary: Trailing comment restates a literal value and its unit.

examples.title: Assertion repeats a constructor keyword
Assertion checks a derived value

limitations: Literal-only assertions owned by Ruff or SARJ057 are excluded.
Constructor echoes with evidence of field coercion are excluded.
Imported constructors are excluded because their assignment, validation, and normalization behavior is not visible.
rules.rationale: Constructor keyword echoes and equivalent tautologies cannot reveal an application defect.
rules.remediation: Assert a transformation, validation result, or other value produced independently of the fixture literal.
rules.summary: Assertions should depend on behavior rather than echoing values supplied by the test.

limitations: Only test paths are analyzed.
Potentially effectful statements between assignments prevent a finding.
rules.rationale: Overwritten or contradicted mock setup adds misleading, unreachable test behavior.

examples.title: Constraint added without scanning existing rows

files.source: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT check_age CHECK (age >= 18);

examples.title: Constraint validated while it is added

limitations: Only PostgreSQL migration files and CHECK or foreign-key constraints added to existing tables are inspected.
rules.rationale: Validating a new CHECK or foreign key while adding it can hold disruptive locks while PostgreSQL scans existing rows.
rules.remediation: Add the constraint as NOT VALID, then validate it in a separate ALTER TABLE statement.
rules.summary: ADD CONSTRAINT (CHECK/FK) without NOT VALID blocks writes during full-table validation.

examples.title: Timestamp with time-zone semantics

rules.rationale: Naive timestamps discard offset context and make cross-time-zone comparisons ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Declare persisted instants as TIMESTAMPTZ or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
rules.summary: TIMESTAMP without TIME ZONE — use TIMESTAMPTZ.

files.source: CREATE TABLE orders (id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY);

examples.title: Table creation that fails on replay

limitations: Dialect-specific DDL forms are checked only where the guard syntax is supported.
rules.rationale: A partially applied migration may be retried, so unconditional object creation or removal can fail before recovery completes.
rules.remediation: Use the supported IF NOT EXISTS or IF EXISTS form for the DDL statement.
rules.summary: DDL without IF [NOT] EXISTS — migrations must be safe to re-run.

files.source: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_idx ON users(email);

examples.title: Concurrent index build

limitations: Indexes on tables created earlier in the same file are exempt because no concurrent writers exist yet.
rules.rationale: Building an index normally blocks writes to an existing PostgreSQL table for the duration of the build.
rules.remediation: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in a nontransactional migration.
rules.summary: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY — locks the table against writes.

examples.title: Seed insert without conflict handling

limitations: Only PostgreSQL migration paths and explicitly marked PostgreSQL migrations are checked.
rules.rationale: A retried seed migration can duplicate rows or fail on a uniqueness constraint when an insert has no replay behavior.
rules.remediation: Add ON CONFLICT with an explicit DO NOTHING or DO UPDATE action.
rules.summary: INSERT without ON CONFLICT — migration data writes must be idempotent upserts.

files.source: SELECT id FROM call ORDER BY id LIMIT 50 OFFSET 100;

examples.title: Pagination that scans skipped rows

limitations: The rule recognizes literal and common driver parameter markers following OFFSET.
rules.rationale: OFFSET scans and discards every skipped row, so later pages become slower as the result set grows.
rules.remediation: Filter on a stable cursor column, preserve its ordering, and retain a bounded LIMIT.
rules.summary: OFFSET pagination — use cursor pagination (WHERE id > :cursor).

examples.title: PostgreSQL enum type
Text column with an explicit value constraint

limitations: PostgreSQL dump files are excluded.
Generated migrations still report, but diagnostics direct the edit to the owning schema model.
rules.rationale: PostgreSQL enums make ordinary value changes operationally awkward and couple application evolution to database type migrations.
rules.remediation: Store the value as TEXT and constrain the allowed values with an explicit CHECK expression.
rules.summary: CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM — use TEXT + CHECK constraint instead.

examples.title: Indexable JSONB column

limitations: PostgreSQL dump files are excluded.
JSON tokens inside comments, string literals, and longer identifiers are ignored.
Query and data-migration casts are excluded because an external or legacy JSON column may require them.
rules.rationale: JSONB supports indexing and containment operators and avoids reparsing the stored document on every read.
rules.remediation: Declare JSONB columns and use jsonb casts for JSON document values.
rules.summary: JSON column type or table-DDL cast — use JSONB.

files.source: CREATE TABLE users (name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(name) <= 255));

examples.title: Text column with an explicit length constraint

limitations: MySQL and SQLite sources are excluded because their VARCHAR behavior differs.
rules.rationale: PostgreSQL gives VARCHAR(n) no storage or performance advantage, while its length cap obscures a business constraint.
rules.remediation: Use TEXT and express a real maximum length with an explicit CHECK constraint when needed.
rules.summary: VARCHAR(n) — use TEXT (+ CHECK length if needed).

files.source: CREATE TABLE call (id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7());

examples.title: Time-ordered UUID default

limitations: uuidv7() requires PostgreSQL 18 or an equivalent extension-provided function.
rules.rationale: Random UUID keys scatter inserts across a B-tree, while time-ordered UUIDv7 values preserve index locality.
rules.remediation: Use the PostgreSQL uuidv7() function for generated UUID defaults and values.
rules.summary: `gen_random_uuid()` emits a random UUIDv4 — use `uuidv7()` so keys are time-ordered.

examples.title: Foreign key without a child-table index

limitations: A bounded scan includes indexes from sibling files in the same migration tree.
rules.rationale: PostgreSQL does not automatically index referencing columns, so parent updates and deletes may scan the child table.
rules.remediation: Create an index whose leading columns cover the foreign-key columns on the child table.
rules.summary: FOREIGN KEY column missing index — causes full-table scans and locks on parent row deletes.

rules.remediation: Set a short positive lock_timeout or statement_timeout before the DDL statement.
rules.summary: DDL migration missing positive SET [LOCAL] lock_timeout or statement_timeout prior to DDL.
